page: Amazon Web Services i8g.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton processors. It features 4 dedicated physical cores based on the arm64 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with 1 thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. The processor allocation includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. System memory is sized at 32.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Storage includes a bundled 937 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No hardware GPU acceleration is included.

Benchmark testing highlights top-tier memory subsystem performance, with a PassMark memory score of 2,984.74 ranking in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 96.68 GB/sec, while write operations sustain 44.62 GB/sec. CPU benchmarks show moderate general execution capabilities, achieving an average stress-ng multi-core score of 6,817.76 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,926.0. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong at 14.26 GB/sec. Conversely, synthetic compute suites evaluate lower, with PassMark CPU score at 3,947.79 and cryptographic tests falling in the bottom decile at 750.86.

The combination of high memory bandwidth, 8 GB of RAM per vCPU, and direct-attached NVMe storage delivers balanced efficiency for IOPS-demanding systems without relying on external block storage. Limitations include reduced compute-bound throughput in instruction-heavy tasks and modest 2 Gbps networking bandwidth. Consequently, the i8g.xlarge is suited for local caching layers, high-throughput Redis deployments, transactional databases, and fast temporary file processing.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.xlarge is a storage-optimized Nitro instance featuring 4 dedicated physical cores based on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V2 architecture clocked at 2.8 GHz. The server provides 32.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8.0 GB per-core density, alongside a bundled 937 GB local NVMe solid-state drive and 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark testing exhibits top-tier memory throughput, scoring in the top 10 percent on PassMark memory evaluations and achieving 96.68 GB/sec in large-block read operations. While general compute performance and compression remain within the median range, cryptographic and synthetic CPU tests show modest output. The balanced hardware ratio and local NVMe capacity render this instance well suited for transactional databases, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, and data-intensive local processing pipelines.
